idiom_name: Hash.default_proc cells keyed by [cell_x, cell_y] arrays
implementation_notes: Ruby's Hash with a default block is the manual realization: Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] } keyed by [cell_x, cell_y] arrays holds the members, and Array#select applies the exact predicate after the candidate cells are visited (ruby-doc Hash). The structure is short and idiomatic, but a mutating default block also allocates on read, so queries over empty cells should use fetch with a default instead. Ruby has no standard spatial index; a heavy numeric workload would delegate to a C-backed gem rather than a pure-Ruby structure.
pitfalls: A default block that mutates the hash turns a read into a write: querying empty cells grows the structure and surprises iterators.
Objects referenced only by the grid are kept alive by it; forgetting to remove despawned entities is a memory leak, not just a stale result.
Array keys hash by value but mutate if reused, so never mutate a key array after using it in the grid.
